August 2, 2026

Trump says he cancelled Iran strike after deal framework agreed

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Trump said the United States was prepared to attack the Islamic Republic of Iran at levels of military force he described as unseen since World War II, but had been asked by Iran and other Middle Eastern countries to hold off because the perimeters of a deal had been agreed. He said the terms would include the immediate, complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. He stated he had agreed to cancel the attack subject to a rapid deal, and that Israel joined him in the commitment. The statement was posted on Truth Social on August 1.

Rubio says visa policy will bar foreign nationals over rhetoric against Israel

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @ericmoutsos

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration has implemented a new visa policy intended to prevent foreign nationals from entering the United States to foment hatred against the Jewish community, and that it is holding international organizations and nations accountable for rhetoric against Israel. Critics said the policy conditions entry to the country on speech about a foreign state rather than on conduct, and would extend to those describing Israeli actions as war crimes. The remarks were delivered alongside statements by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressing American supporters, who urged them to stand up against what he called a rising tide of antisemitism.

Pentagon accounts invoke scripture in recruitment push as Iran escalation looms

tags: defense, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Multiple Department of Defense accounts, including that of Sean Parnell, posted scriptural appeals urging Americans to enlist, quoting Isaiah 6:8: "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? And I said, here I am, send me." The posts were amplified by the Department of War account. The messaging is described as part of a redesigned Pentagon communications approach framing overseas military service in religious terms, and came as the United States weighed a major escalation against Iran.

Trump breaks with his own Justice Department over reflecting pool case

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro filed a motion to dismiss charges against an Olympian over alleged vandalism of the reflecting pool, stating in a court filing that there was no evidence of vandalism and that the damage resulted from poor contractor work. Trump publicly disagreed on Truth Social, writing that he disagreed 100 percent with Pirro, that he did not know what she was thinking, and that the major damage was caused by vandals who emblazoned "86 47" on the grass. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum also contradicted the Justice Department, saying evidence was clear that vandals repeatedly damaged the pool, that some were caught on camera, and that expert and eyewitness testimony had been provided.

Capital One says it closed Trump accounts over suspicious transactions

tags: legal, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

In a court filing in the Southern District of Florida, Capital One said it shut down Donald Trump's bank accounts in 2021 after months of analysis by its anti-money laundering professionals identified suspicious transaction patterns, and that the decision was made under federal anti-money laundering obligations. The filing responds to a lawsuit brought by the trust that oversees Trump's businesses, which alleged the accounts were unjustly closed. Trump has long claimed banks closed accounts belonging to conservatives for political reasons.

Trump Media launches paid early-access feed of Truth Social posts

tags: markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump Media has launched Truth API, a paid data service offering firms a direct, licensed, real-time feed of what it calls the platform's most market-moving posts. The service costs as much as $100,000 a month. Analysts said the arrangement gives paying financial firms advance access to presidential statements that move markets, including on the war, before the general public sees them, and characterized it as market manipulation.

Corporations receive over $100 billion in tariff refunds after Supreme Court ruling

tags: markets, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

The federal government has paid out more than $100 billion in tariff refunds to companies after the Supreme Court invalidated Trump's tariffs. Amazon received $600 million in refunds in the past quarter and Apple received $2 billion. The promised tariff dividend checks to the American public are not being issued, leaving it to individual companies to decide whether to pass any refund on to consumers.

RFK Jr declines to say how US would prevent a future pandemic

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Asked by Dana Bash how the United States would prevent a future pandemic, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. discussed past failures, saying the country did everything wrong during COVID. Pressed on current preparations, he said constitutional rights must be protected and argued that rights were dismantled during the pandemic, and he blamed the media for the crisis. He did not set out a plan for pandemic prevention.

Spokane wildfires destroy hundreds of buildings as evacuations continue

tags: climate
sources: @aaronparnas

Wildfires burning in and around Spokane, Washington have placed most of the city under a level three evacuation order, with more than 40,000 people without power. Wildfires across the state are burning more than 250,000 acres, and the local fire department reports that hundreds of buildings have been destroyed or damaged, potentially upwards of 600, many of them homes. Residents in many areas remain under evacuation warnings, and the federal government has not yet commented.

Three dead in mass shooting at Idaho restaurant

tags: policing, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Three people were confirmed dead and two injured in a shooting at an In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho on the evening of August 1. According to NBC News the shooter is dead and shelter-in-place orders have been lifted. Video circulating shows a man with an AR-15 style weapon opening fire. The United States has recorded more mass shootings than days in the year.

New Texas law makes non-compliant THC possession a felony

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Under a new Texas state law, possession of THC products that do not comply with the new regulations is a state jail felony. Possession of under one gram carries 180 days to two years in jail and a fine of up to $10,000, while up to four grams is a third-degree felony carrying up to 10 years. Up to 400 grams carries up to 20 years, and more than 400 grams carries up to a life sentence and a fine of up to $50,000.

Israel removes Spanish representatives from coordination centre

tags: politics, war
sources: @ericmoutsos

Israel announced the removal of Spain's representatives from the coordination centre in Kiryat Gat, saying it would not stay silent in the face of those attacking it after Spain repeatedly took positions against Israel. The move follows Spanish criticism of the conduct of Israeli forces. Commentary accompanying the announcement questioned the funding behind organised movements of refugees toward European shores.
